name: Destroy the Legion
summary: Valusha at Splintertree Post orders Horde champions to strike back against lingering Burning Legion forces threatening the Warsong Lumber Camp. Lingering demons gather in the scarred canyons and hills of eastern Ashenvale, where Mannoroth once met his end.

sections.title: A Lingering Corruption
sections.body: Though the Third War saw the defeat of the Burning Legion at Mount Hyjal, remnants of the demonic host still fester in Ashenvale's eastern ridges. The ground surrounding Felfire Hill, Demon Fall Canyon, and Demon Fall Ridge remains blistered by fel energy, sustaining roaming felguards, fiery infernals, and ravenous lashers. These fiends frequently raid Horde operations, menacing the vital logging efforts of the Warsong Outriders.

sections.title: Securing the Lumber Camp
sections.body: The Warsong Lumber Camp is essential for supplying timber to build and fortify Orgrimmar. Demon incursions threaten not only the laborers but also the strategic foothold the Horde fights to maintain against the night elves. Stationed at Splintertree Post, Valusha directs warriors to thin the demonic ranks directly at their gathering grounds, crushing the assault before the lumber camp is overrun.

faq.q: Why are there demons in Ashenvale?
faq.answer: During the Third War, the pit lord Mannoroth corrupted these lands with demonic blood, and the Legion staged massive armies throughout the forest. Although Archimonde was destroyed at Mount Hyjal, scattered demons, roving felguards, and summoned infernals still haunt the scarred eastern ridges.

Valusha is an orc warrior stationed at Splintertree Post. Fierce and aggressive, she coordinates strikes against threats encroaching on Horde holdings in Ashenvale, holding particular contempt for both demons and Alliance interlopers.

faq.q: Where are the demons attacking from?
faq.answer: The demons stage their attacks from the corrupted eastern reaches of Ashenvale, specifically across Felfire Hill, Demon Fall Canyon, and Demon Fall Ridge, just south and east of the main road.

faq.q: Why does the Horde care about these demons?
faq.answer: Demonic warbands regularly raid the Warsong Lumber Camp. The timber gathered there is critical for constructing Orgrimmar and maintaining the Horde's presence, making any disruption an existential threat to their war effort in Kalimdor.

faq.q: What is the history behind Demon Fall Canyon?
faq.answer: Demon Fall Canyon is the historic site where Grommash Hellscream and Thrall confronted the pit lord Mannoroth. Grom struck down the demon lord at the cost of his own life, freeing the orcish race from the blood curse. The surrounding terrain still bears the taint of Mannoroth's dying burst of fel power.

faq.q: What kinds of demons are being targeted?
faq.answer: The task focuses on eliminating the front-line shock troops of the remnants: brutal Roaming Felguards, animated Searing Infernals, and the fel-infused plant horrors known as Mannoroc Lashers.

angles.text: Defending the Warsong Lumber Camp preserves the Horde's principal source of construction timber in Kalimdor while asserting military strength in Ashenvale.
For orcs, slaying demons in the very canyons where Grommash Hellscream died defeating Mannoroth is both a matter of personal honor and proof of their hard-won freedom from the blood curse.
Facing massive felguards and searing stone infernals offers frontline combatants a brutal test of resolve against adversaries far more resilient than woodland sentinels.
The chaotic concentrations of roaming demons and fel energy in eastern Ashenvale provide a firsthand look at unsupervised Legion remnants running wild without a master.
